newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ulster Bank half-yr pre-tax profit up 6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Ulster Bank half-yr pre-tax profit up 6 pct.

text.p: Ulster Bank, the Irish subsidiary of National Westminster Bank Plc, said on Tuesday that pre-tax profit for the half-year to June 30 rose to 70 million sterling from 66 million a year earlier.
Ulster Bank said in a statement that it achieved good growth in income which rose to 181 million from 171 million, largely due to increased lending and treasury operations.
Total costs rose to 105 million from 99 million, reflecting higher staff and administration costs but the bank's provision for bad debts was unchanged.
Ulster Bank said it remained at historically low levels due to the buoyant economies in both the Republic of Ireland and in Northern Ireland.
Total group lending rose by 271 million in the first half to 4.338 billion.
Ulster Bank said its cost income ratio increased to 58.0 from 57.9 in the first half of 1996 but was down from 59.8 percent in the second half of last year.
The bank said its retail division reported a five percent increase in profits to 40 million sterling.
"Lending was substantially higher with growth of 12 percent but margins fell, reflecting strong competition for business," it said.
The market division reported a seven percent increase in profits to 30 million with all businesses producing higher results despite the adverse affect of the strength of sterling, Ulster Bank said.
